title: Injured Emigre Reported Better

page_data.en:
SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE
S. S. R. G.
No. S. B. D. 5422 (6)
Date 14 3 40

Injured Emigre
Reported Better

Ward Rd. Row Talked
In Refugee Homes;
Officials Deny

While Mr. J. Wissler, emigre
camp official at Ward Road, is
recovering from the blows which
he sustained at the hands of 130
dissenting refugees at the camp
on Saturday, a morning journal
today added another denial to the
long list already made by com-
mittee officials that any outbreak
had taken place.
"Of course there was no fight-
ing or trouble on Saturday be-
cause that was our Sabbath," Mr.
Julius Weinberger, chief of the
emigre camp at Ward Road ex-
claimed this morning in denying
the report and "backing up" his
statements made to a morning
paper.

Verbal Blows
To the morning newspaper Mr.
Weinberger had declared: "The
whole report was a strongly im-
aginative exaggeration of a little
incident which occurred on Fri-
day, the previous day and con-
sisted of a few 'troublesome men'
expressing with voices, not fists,
dissatisfaction of general living
conditions in the camp."
Mr. Weinberger omitted mak-
ing any mention of the refugee
committee's intention to force
about 130 emigres living in Ward
Road camp to move to the hostel
in Pingliang Road.

Main Topic
Despite the refutation given by
Mr. Weinberger and the refusal
of the European Jewish Refugee
Committee to issue any statement
on the matter, emigres residing
north of the creek continued to
discuss the incident as one of
the main topics in homes and
cafes last night, while an emigre
paper permitted brief mention to
appear that the trouble had been
temporarily settled.
The Shanghai Evening Post's
report of the affair which ap-
peared yesterday was to the effect
that a disturbance had taken
place shortly after the tiffin meal
on Saturday at the Ward Road
refugee camp, involving 130 per-
sons who refused to comply with
orders from the committee to
transfer to the Pingliang Road
camp.

Police Warned
In the ensuing trouble, one of
the camp officials was injured by
blows. Further disturbance was
anticipated on Sunday and the
police were warned, but the dan-
ger was averted when emigre
officials decided to postpone the
"moving day" order another
week.
Mr. Weinberger emphasized in
his conversation with the Even-
ing Post this morning that he
had been an officer during the
World War and therefore held
his word sacred. He inferred
that he would not lie about such
matters.

上海公共租界工部局警务处
S. S. R. G.
编号 S. B. D. 5422 (6)
日期 1940年3月14日

受伤流亡者
据报情况好转

华德路难民营发生口角；
官员予以否认

当华德路（Ward Road）流亡者营地官员 J. Wissler 先生正从周六在营地遭受130名持异议流亡者殴打所致的伤势中恢复时，一家晨报今日又增添了一项否认声明，加入了该委员会官员此前已作出的一长串否认发生任何暴乱的行列。
“当然，周六没有发生打斗或麻烦，因为那是我们的安息日，”华德路流亡者营地主管 Julius Weinberger 先生今晨在否认该报道并“支持”他此前向一家晨报所作的陈述时惊呼道。

言语冲突
Weinberger 先生对该晨报宣称：“整篇报道是对前一天（周五）发生的一起小事件的极具想象力的夸大，该事件仅涉及少数‘麻烦人物’用声音而非拳头表达对营地总体生活条件的不满。”
Weinberger 先生只字未提流亡者委员会意图迫使居住在华德路营地的约130名流亡者迁往平凉路（Pingliang Road）招待所一事。

主要话题
尽管 Weinberger 先生予以驳斥，且欧洲犹太难民委员会拒绝就此事项发表任何声明，但昨晚，住在苏州河以北的流亡者仍在住所和咖啡馆中将此事件作为主要话题进行讨论，而一份流亡者报纸则允许刊登简短提及，称麻烦已暂时平息。
《上海晚邮报》（Shanghai Evening Post）昨日关于此事的报道大意是：周六午餐后不久，华德路难民营发生了一起骚乱，涉及130名拒绝服从委员会命令迁往平凉路营地的人员。

警方获预警
在随后的混乱中，一名营地官员被殴致伤。预计周日会发生进一步的骚乱，警方已接到警告，但当流亡者官员决定将“搬迁日”命令再推迟一周时，危险得以避免。
Weinberger 先生在今晨与《晚邮报》的谈话中强调，他曾在世界大战期间担任军官，因此视自己的话语为神圣。他暗示自己不会在此类事情上撒谎。
